title: A click on the empty canvas past the frame lets go of a zoomed recording
goal: With a recording pushed in to 220% and picked, clicking the empty canvas just outside the frame keeps the recording picked, because its magnified picture reaches out there even though nothing of it is drawn. A click on empty canvas should let go of it, the way it does for anything else.
notes: Reproduced 2026-10-12 by a-zoomed-recording-shows-its-ring-on-the-frame-n. Script: the steps of Scripts/playtest/framing-a-zoom-keys-its-centre-walk.json up to snapshot 2-zoomed-at-5, then {click at [-20,400] space document}, wait, {expectPicked layers []}. Ran: Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/ringcheck/offcanvas-click-walk.json --no-build. Output: "[30 expectPicked] FAILED: the layers picked are Tutorial Sample, not nothing". Cause: the canvas hit test reads the POSED document (canvasGeometryDocument), where the pushed-in clip frame is 2816 wide, and nothing clips it to the canvas. The outline now rings the frame (PhotonzDocument.frameRing), so the hit should agree: a timed picture grown past its own box should not be hit outside the canvas. Entry points: PhotonzDocument.hitTest / canvasHitTest (LayerGrouping.swift), CanvasNSView.groupAwarePick.
acceptance: With the sample recording at 220% and picked, a click on the empty canvas 20 points left of the frame leaves nothing picked
A click on the picture inside the frame still picks the recording and a drag there still frames the shot
A walk at Next defaults proves both
